classification.difficultyReason: 1G Q72: Structural selection, multiple connected steps, proof or admissible-case reasoning. Factorisation and inadmissible-root rejection are taught; repeated squaring of several radicals is an approved extension.

answer.short:
$x=7$.

Square twice, retaining $x\geq1$ after isolating the remaining radical; check the root.
answer.worked:
The original domain is $x\geq-\frac{7}{6}$. Squaring gives
$$\begin{align*}2x+11+2\sqrt{(x+2)(x+9)}&=6x+7\\\sqrt{(x+2)(x+9)}&=2x-2.\end{align*}$$
Thus $x\geq1$. Squaring again,
$$\begin{align*}(x+2)(x+9)&=(2x-2)^2\\x^2+11x+18&=4x^2-8x+4\\3x^2-19x-14&=0\\(3x+2)(x-7)&=0\\x&=-\frac23\text{ or }7.\end{align*}$$
Reject $-\frac{2}{3}$ because $x\geq1$. Check $x=7$: $\sqrt9+\sqrt{16}=3+4=\sqrt{49}$. Hence $x=7$.
